t: How to write a reason In an exam, the answer and the reason are marked separately. The reason is usually a C1 mark: it is lost if you write only the angle. Write the angle you found, then a short reason in words, using the standard wording. Not it is a circle rule or same arc. Say the whole fact. You will also use simpler reasons: angles in a triangle add up to one hundred and eighty degrees, angles on a straight line add up to one hundred and eighty degrees, angles in a quadrilateral add up to three hundred and sixty degrees, and the base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal (two radii make an isosceles triangle). Example: seventy-eight is divisible by six because seventy-eight divided by six equals thirteen. four thousand, five hundred and sixty-three is divisible by three because its digits add up to eighteen, which is a multiple of three. t: Elimination. A way to solve simultaneous equations. Add or subtract the two equations so that one letter disappears, leaving one equation with one unknown. You may need to multiply an equation first so that the numbers in front of the letter match. Examples: x plus y equals seven and x minus y equals one. If the signs are different, add. Multiply every term of an equation, including the number on the right. Flip it: Check an answer by putting it back into both original equations.

Example, two flips of a fair coin, the probability of head then head equals the fraction 1 over 2, times the fraction 1 over 2, equals the fraction 1 over 4.

t: Truncation. Cutting off the digits after a chosen place without rounding. Examples: seven point three eight truncated to one decimal place is seven point three (rounding would give seven point four). If a number is four point six after truncation to one d.p., then four point six is less than or equal to x is less than four point seven. Watch out: The original number is at least the truncated value and less than one rounding unit above it, so the error interval is not half a unit each way.

t: Turning point. The point where a graph changes direction: a minimum if it goes down then up, a maximum if it goes up then down. Example: For y equals (x minus p) squared plus q the turning point is p comma q.
